title: Vanishing for a nontrivial algebraically trivial line module
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that $L$ is algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O_A$ but $L\not\cong\mathcal O_A$. Here algebraic equivalence is the equivalence relation generated by pairs of fibres of invertible-module families over connected smooth parameter varieties, as in [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus]. For every integer $i\geq0$, the coherent Zariski sheaf cohomology group $H^i(A,L)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is zero. This holds in every characteristic and in every dimension, including dimension zero.

source.place: Mumford, Abelian Varieties, II §8, property (vii), printed p.76 (argument concluding on p.77). The initial properties (i)–(vii) precede the characteristic-zero construction and hold in every characteristic. Primary book scan read online at https://djvu.online/file/2tC7xp3dbqGCh; local book WANTED.

proof.text:
The scheme $A$ is geometrically integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] and commutative by [lem-sc-av-commutative]. It is proper and smooth by [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Thus it is quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]; smoothness supplies local finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], hence finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. This base is locally Noetherian (the only ideals of a field are $0,k$), and its geometric fibre is an abelian variety by geometric integrality and smoothness. The representing property is tested on every geometric fibre $A_\Omega$, $\Omega\supseteq k$ algebraically closed. Take a chain of links from $L$ to $\mathcal O_A$ as in the item. For one link, a family $\mathcal M$ over a connected smooth parameter variety $V/k$ with fibres $\mathcal M_{v_1},\mathcal M_{v_2}$ at $v_1,v_2\in V(k)$, the base change to $A_\Omega\times V_\Omega$ is such a family over $V_\Omega$ with fibres the base changes: $V_\Omega$ is smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] (1) (the relative dimension is locally constant [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], hence constant on connected $V$) and connected by [lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected], since an algebraically closed $k$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]. Link by link, $L_\Omega$ is algebraically trivial. Choose a basis of the one-dimensional fibre $L|_0$. The representing property gives $b\in A^\vee(k)$ and $L\simeq\mathcal P_A|_{A\times\{b\}}$. Restrict the first biadditivity identity of that node to $b$. Its explicit correspondence between line modules on a scheme and ordinary invertible modules gives, on the Zariski scheme $A\times_kA$,
$$m^*L\simeq p_1^*L\otimes p_2^*L.$$
Here $m$ is addition and $p_1,p_2$ are the projections. This is precisely Mumford II §8 (i),(vi), for the algebraic-equivalence convention of the item.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4 and Remark 8.5, printed pp.35–36; Mumford II §8 (i),(vi), pp.75–76; existing relative Poincare statement specialized to a field

proof.text: Let $\iota=[-1]:A\to A$. Pull the identity of step 1 back along $(1,\iota):A\to A\times_kA$. Pullback composition [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] and tensor compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] identify the right side with $L\otimes\iota^*L$. The left side is the pullback of $L$ along the constant zero map, hence the constant line $\mathcal O_A\otimes_kL|_0$. The chosen basis therefore gives $L\otimes\iota^*L\simeq\mathcal O_A$.

source.place: II §8 (ii),(iii), printed p.75; inversion specialization used in (vii), p.76

proof.text: Suppose $0\ne s\in H^0(A,L)=\Gamma(A,L)$. On an integral scheme a nonzero section of an invertible module is nonzero at the generic point: in a local frame its coefficient is a regular function in a domain, and vanishing generically makes that coefficient zero. Thus $s$ and $\iota^*s$ are both nonzero generically. Their tensor, under step 2, is a nonzero global function. By [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] (2), $\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)=k$, so that function is a nonzero scalar. At every point, the two local coefficients have product a unit; each is consequently a unit. Hence $s$ is everywhere a generator and trivializes $L$, contrary to the hypothesis. We have proved $H^0(A,L)=0$. This argument uses only the local rank-one description [def-sc-invertible-module], not a vanishing theorem for divisors.

source.place: II §8 (vii), printed p.76: effective-divisor argument, written in local rank-one frames

proof.text:
We prove $H^n(A,L)=0$ by strong induction on $n\geq0$, with base case step 3. Suppose $n>0$ and the assertion holds below $n$. Apply [lem-sc-picard-kunneth-qcoh] to $X=Y=A$, $F=G=L$. Its hypotheses hold: $L$ is quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module]; properness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence affine diagonal by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] (b), using the diagonal definition in [def-weil-proper-morphism] and quasi-compactness in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. It yields
$$H^n(A\times_kA,p_1^*L\otimes p_2^*L)\cong\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^p(A,L)\otimes_kH^q(A,L)=0.$$
Indeed $p,q\geq0$ and $p+q=n>0$ imply $p<n$ or $q<n$, so an induction hypothesis kills one factor in every summand. The coefficient isomorphism in step 1 therefore gives $H^n(A\times_kA,m^*L)=0$.

source.place: II §8 (vii), printed pp.76–77; Stacks Tag 0BED, varieties-lemma-kunneth

proof.text:
Set $j:A\to A\times_kA$, $x\mapsto(x,0)$. Then $m\circ j=1_A$. By the composition clause of [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial], the composite
$$H^n(A,L)\xrightarrow{m^*}H^n(A\times_kA,m^*L)\xrightarrow{j^*}H^n(A,j^*m^*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^n(A,L)$$
is the identity: use the canonical pullback comparison for $m\circ j=1_A$, not an arbitrarily chosen line-bundle trivialization. The middle group is zero by step 4, so its composite is zero. Thus the identity of $H^n(A,L)$ is zero and this group vanishes, completing the induction. Nothing in these steps divides by the characteristic or assumes positive dimension; dimension zero is included.

tool_uses.why: Geometric integrality of an abelian variety is needed for the generic-section argument; the six-functor unit does not give this geometric fact.
Commutativity verifies the hypothesis of the existing relative Poincare calculus; it is a general abelian-variety tool.

Use its representing property and its first displayed biadditivity identity at a k-point to obtain the multiplicative line-bundle identity, a coherent Picard tool independent of the six-functor route.
Canonical composition of ordinary module pullbacks is needed to restrict the line-bundle identity; no six-functor unit lemma replaces this elementary sheaf-theoretic tool.
Tensor compatibility of ordinary module pullback identifies the antidiagonal restriction, independently of constructible coefficient operations.
Its second clause identifies global functions on a proper geometrically integral scheme with the base field, used to show a nonzero section trivializes L.
Its clause (b) makes the closed relative diagonal affine, verifying the hypothesis of coherent Kunneth.
Use coherent Zariski Kunneth over a field, not etale or condensed-coefficient Kunneth, for the two line-bundle factors.
The explicit ordinary module cohomology composition rule makes pullback along addition split injective via its identity section.
Clause (1): base change of the smooth parameter varieties to a geometric fibre, to verify algebraic triviality on every geometric fibre of A over Spec k (reviewer FIX).
Connected parameter varieties over the algebraically closed k stay connected after base change to a geometric fibre (reviewer FIX).

The representing property, the first biadditivity identity and the line-module correspondence are in that node's statement, and the restriction to b gives m*L≅p1*L⊗p2*L. FIX (E1): the representing property needs L algebraically trivial on every geometric fibre A_Ω, which was not checked. These are added to uses, proof_deps and tool_uses; the step is 1981 characters. Step 2: pullback along (1,[-1]) gives L⊗ι*L≅O_A, correct. Step 3: a nonzero s gives a nonzero section s⊗ι*s, which is constant by lem-pc-h0-proper-variety(2), so s trivializes L; this is the only use of non-triviality and it is needed. Step 4: Künneth hypotheses hold (affine diagonal by closed-immersion(b)); the strong induction is set up correctly, endpoints included.
